subject: math

objective.text: Solve word problems involving different combinations of coins with the same total value.

explanations.title: Different coins, same value
explanations.text: Different coins can make the same value. A dime and 5 pennies is 15 cents. 3 nickels is also 15 cents.

explanations.title: Show an amount two ways
explanations.text: To show an amount two ways, use different coins. 28 cents is a quarter and 3 pennies. It is also 2 dimes and 8 pennies.

explanations.title: Trade coins
explanations.text: You can trade coins for other coins of the same value. Trade a quarter for 2 dimes and a nickel. The total stays the same.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 2 (S: I traded each of my quarters for 2 dimes and a nickel)

explanations.title: Tape diagram of coins
explanations.text: A tape diagram can show the value of each kind of coin as a part. The parts add up to the total value.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 2 (S: A tape diagram with one part 40 cents, one part 25 cents, and one part 10 cents)

explanations.title: Write the coins and the value
explanations.text: Write the coins you used and the total value. For example, 8 dimes and 3 pennies is 83 cents.

examples.title: 15 cents two ways
examples.text: A dime and 5 pennies is 15 cents. 3 nickels is 15 cents. The values are equal.

examples.title: Tony's 83 cents
examples.text: 8 dimes and 3 pennies is 83 cents. 3 quarters, 1 nickel and 3 pennies is also 83 cents.

examples.title: Carla and Peyton
examples.text: Carla has 4 dimes, 1 quarter and 2 nickels. That is 75 cents. Peyton has 3 coins with the same value. 25 plus 25 plus 25 is 75. Peyton has 3 quarters.

visual_generation_rules: Diffusion cannot count reliably. Any picture where an exact number of objects matters must be built by code (SVG or widget) or drawn by an artist.
Diffusion is allowed only for: style or background art, and single icons (one ball, one pencil, one leaf, one character) that code then tiles to the exact count.
Every visual must be checked by a person: the count shown must equal the stimulus in the question and the rubric answer key.
Animations are described as frames with exact counts per frame, so they can be built or generated and then checked frame by frame.
Visual explanations are valid only when the asset exists (pipeline doc, Planner rules).
